nodes.title: Dominance order on partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda = [\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_L]$ be a finite list of natural numbers, with $L \ge 0$. Its conjugate $\lambda'$ is the empty list if $L = 0$, and otherwise the list $[\lambda'_1, \dots, \lambda'_{\lambda_1}]$ of length $\lambda_1$ with $\lambda'_j = \#\{i : 1 \le i \le L,\ \lambda_i \ge j\}$ for $1 \le j \le \lambda_1$. The list $\lambda$ is self-conjugate when $\lambda' = \lambda$.
nodes.title: Self-conjugate partition

nodes.summary: A finite list $d = [d_1, \dots, d_m]$ of natural numbers is unimodal when $d_i \ge 1$ for every $i$ and there is an index $j$ with $1 \le j \le m$ such that $d_1 \le d_2 \le \dots \le d_j$ and $d_j \ge d_{j+1} \ge \dots \ge d_m$. In particular a unimodal list has $m \ge 1$, so the empty list is not unimodal; for $j = 1$ the first condition is vacuous and for $j = m$ the second is.

nodes.title: Conjugate partition

nodes.summary: Let $j, k, n \ge 0$ be integers. A partition of $n$ is a finite multiset of positive integers whose sum is $n$; the empty partition is the unique partition of $0$. Then $p(j, k, n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ with at most $k$ parts, counted with multiplicity, each of which is at most $j$. In particular $p(j, k, 0) = 1$ for all $j$ and $k$, while $p(0, k, n) = p(j, 0, n) = 0$ for $n \ge 1$.

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 0$ be an integer. A partition $\lambda$ is a finite multiset of positive integers, and its weight $|\lambda|$ is the sum of its parts. A V-partition of weight $n$ is a triple $(c, \lambda, \mu)$ in which $c \ge 0$ is an integer, $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are partitions all of whose parts are at most $c$, and $c + |\lambda| + |\mu| = n$.
